hero.disclaimer: Unofficial fan tool. Not affiliated with CD PROJEKT RED. Remastered PC, patch 5.01.
callout.close2: The app never overwrites a save; it writes a new file next to your own. Keep a backup of your saves folder anyway.
safety.title: Safety notes
safety.lede: What the app does to your files, and what it leaves alone.
safety.l1: The app never overwrites a save. It writes a new file (plus small sidecar files) and refuses if the name exists.
safety.l2: Close the game before you export or touch the saves folder.
safety.l4: Steam Cloud may bring old saves back or restore deleted ones. If your Load list looks wrong, pause Cloud sync for The Witcher 3 while you test.
safety.lim1: Unofficial; not affiliated with or endorsed by CD PROJEKT RED.
safety.lim2: Tested on patch 5.01 only. Mods and other patches are not supported.
safety.lim3: Scenes that already happened are not replayed; the save only says they happened.
safety.lim4: Only story decisions are written: facts, quest log and quest graph. Rewards and map pins are not.
safety.lim5: Some decisions are left for you to play in the game. The question screen tells you when this applies.

export.title: Export
export.lede: Builds a new save from your template with your choices applied, checks it, then writes it. Existing files are never overwritten.

export.unfinished.other: {n} of your choices are not finished yet.
export.unfinished.rest: Export will refuse them. Check still shows what would happen; go back and pick another answer or skip that quest.
export.noeffects: Nothing: your choices carry no effects yet, so the template is re-packed unchanged.
export.remap.note: — lets a donor whose name table differs from the save’s be copied. Tested in game for one case only.
export.gamedir.note: Your Witcher 3 install (read only). Choices marked “built from the game’s quest data” need it; empty = the Steam default shown.
export.dest.game: This is the game’s own save folder: the new save appears in Load Game.

edit.nav.label: Edit mode
edit.busy: Building the new save and checking it...
edit.list.lede: Pick one of your own saves. It is only read: every change is written as a new save, so the original stays exactly as it is.
edit.list.none: No saves found in this folder.
edit.list.folders.note: Edit mode compares the save with the story using the quest graphs of your Witcher 3 install and the template saves named in the questbook. Both are only read. The first comparison takes a few minutes and is remembered afterwards.
edit.plan.lede: Each quest below is marked from the save's own facts: done, next in line, still ahead, or unclear. The answer the save already holds is shown in italics. Change one and the old answer is rewritten in a new copy of the save.
edit.plan.loading: Comparing the save with the story...
edit.plan.loading.sub: The first time takes a few minutes: every answer of every part of the story is rebuilt once and remembered, so the next saves open at once.
edit.plan.failed: The save could not be compared with the story.
edit.tile.story.sub: {active} next in line, {ahead} still ahead, {unclear} unclear
edit.tile.position.sub: the latest template whose rules apply
edit.answer.unknown: Not known: the save's facts do not tell.
edit.fromregistry: Read from the template list, not from this save's facts.
edit.nochoices.done: Done in this save. Nothing to decide.
edit.nochoices.active: Next in line. Nothing to decide.
edit.active.hint: This part is still ahead of the save. Pick an answer and the save is moved through it; the other choices of these quests take their defaults.
